central_claim: This is an in-silico assessment of whether the published FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis is internally consistent in public data and transfers to EMC; it grades WEAK (the transcriptional shadow is not seen) and explicitly makes no efficacy/potency/clinical claim.

p1s.summary: Several rounded values sit at or just past the conventional half-up rounding boundary (e.g. GSE24369 DNA-damage-checkpoint raw delta 0.0445 printed as '+0.045' rather than '+0.044'; RPL5 panel_sd 0.3465 printed as '0.347'; NR4A1/NR4A3 fold '196.784/13.332=14.76' printed as '15x'). Every instance I checked is defensible under standard round-half-away-from-zero and none changes a qualitative reading, but the document has no stated rounding convention and no regenerating guard on the rounding step itself, so a future artifact regeneration that shifts a delta by a few units in the last decimal could silently flip a printed rounded value without any test catching it.
p1s.evidence: emc-atr-vulnerability.json part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz'].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma.DNA_damage_checkpoint.delta_a_minus_b = 0.0445 (paper prints '+0.045'); part_c_coordinated_dependency.per_gene.RPL5.panel_sd = 0.3465 (paper prints '0.347'); atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json emc_model_identity_check.emc_labelled_samples[0]: NR4A1_TPM 196.784 / NR4A3_TPM 13.332 = 14.76x (paper prints '15x').
p1s.fix: Not required for this commit (all values recompute correctly to the printed precision under ordinary rounding and no conclusion depends on the rounding direction). If a guard is wanted, add a regeneration test that re-derives each rounded display value from the artifact float and fails if the printed digit would change under either round-half-up or round-half-even, so a future artifact drift that crosses a rounding boundary is caught rather than silently accepted.
